name: Paracetamol 500mg
description: A common over-the-counter pain reliever and fever reducer. Effective for mild to moderate pain.
typicalUse: 1-2 tablets every 4-6 hours as needed. Maximum 4g (8 tablets) per day.
storage: Store at room temperature (15-25°C). Keep in original packaging away from moisture.
warning: Do not exceed recommended dose. Overdose can cause serious liver damage. Consult doctor if symptoms persist beyond 3 days.

name: Ibuprofen 400mg
description: A non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drug (NSAID) used to treat pain and inflammation. NOT for fever - use Paracetamol 500mg for fever.
typicalUse: 1 tablet every 4-6 hours with food or milk. Maximum 1200mg (3 tablets) per day for OTC use.
storage: Store at room temperature. Protect from light and moisture.
warning: Take with food to reduce stomach upset. Long-term use may increase risk of heart or kidney problems.

name: Diclofenac Sodium 50mg
description: A potent NSAID used for moderate to severe pain and inflammation associated with conditions like arthritis.
typicalUse: 1 tablet 2-3 times daily with food. As directed by physician.
storage: Store below 30°C. Protect from moisture.
warning: Prescription required for higher doses. May increase cardiovascular risk with long-term use.

name: Aceclofenac 100mg
description: An NSAID with improved gastrointestinal tolerability compared to older NSAIDs. Used for pain and inflammation.
typicalUse: 1 tablet twice daily with food.
storage: Store in a cool, dry place below 25°C.
warning: Use with caution in elderly patients. Monitor kidney function with prolonged use.

name: Naproxen 250mg
description: A long-acting NSAID providing extended relief from pain, inflammation, and fever.
typicalUse: 1-2 tablets twice daily with food or milk.
storage: Store at room temperature. Protect from light.
warning: Has longer duration of action. Take with food to minimize GI side effects.

name: Ketorolac Tromethamine 10mg
description: A powerful short-term NSAID for the management of moderately severe acute pain.
typicalUse: 1 tablet every 4-6 hours. Maximum duration of use: 5 days only.
storage: Store at controlled room temperature.
warning: SHORT-TERM USE ONLY (max 5 days). High risk of serious gastrointestinal adverse events.

name: Etoricoxib 60mg
description: A selective COX-2 inhibitor with potent anti-inflammatory and analgesic activity.
typicalUse: 1 tablet once daily. Dose varies by condition as prescribed.
storage: Store below 30°C. Protect from moisture and light.
warning: Cardiovascular risk assessment required before initiating. Not recommended for patients with established heart disease.

name: Celecoxib 200mg
description: A selective COX-2 NSAID used primarily for osteoarthritis and rheumatoid arthritis with reduced GI side effects.
typicalUse: 1-2 capsules daily as directed by physician.
storage: Store at 20-25°C. Keep in tight container.
warning: May increase risk of serious cardiovascular events. Use lowest effective dose for shortest duration.

name: Meloxicam 15mg
description: A preferential COX-2 inhibitor used for the relief of pain and inflammation in rheumatic conditions.
typicalUse: 1 tablet once daily with food.
storage: Store at room temperature. Protect from light.
warning: Use with caution in patients with history of GI disease. Monitor renal function in elderly.

name: Piroxicam 20mg
description: A long-acting oxicam NSAID used once daily for the symptomatic treatment of various painful conditions.
typicalUse: 1 capsule once daily with food.
storage: Store in airtight container below 30°C.
warning: Not recommended as first-line therapy. Higher GI risk compared to newer NSAIDs. Restricted to short courses.

name: Indomethacin 25mg
description: A potent NSAID with strong anti-inflammatory properties, particularly useful in gout and specific rheumatologic conditions.
typicalUse: 1 capsule 2-3 times daily with food or antacids.
storage: Store below 30°C. Protect from light.
warning: High incidence of frontal headache. Take with meals or antacids to reduce GI distress.

name: Mefenamic Acid 500mg
description: An anthranilic acid derivative NSAID commonly used for menstrual pain and mild to moderate pain.
typicalUse: 1 tablet 3 times daily after meals. Max 7 days of continuous use.
storage: Store in tight, light-resistant container.
warning: If diarrhea occurs, discontinue use. Not for long-term use. Restricted to 7 days maximum.

name: Lornoxicam 8mg
description: A newer oxicam NSAID with rapid onset of action and balanced analgesic/anti-inflammatory effects.
typicalUse: 1 tablet 2-3 times daily with food.
storage: Store below 25°C in original packaging.
warning: Use lowest effective dose. Caution in patients at risk for GI bleeding or cardiovascular events.

name: Dexketoprofen 25mg
description: The active dextrorotatory enantiomer of ketoprofen with rapid onset and potent analgesic activity.
typicalUse: 1 tablet every 8 hours. Take with food.
storage: Store in a cool dry place below 30°C.
warning: Rapid onset of action (30 min). Not recommended for children under 18 without medical advice.

name: Tramadol Hydrochloride 50mg
description: A centrally-acting synthetic opioid analgesic used for moderate to moderately severe pain.
typicalUse: 1-2 tablets every 4-6 hours as prescribed. Maximum 400mg per day.
storage: Store at room temperature. Controlled substance - store securely.
warning: Risk of seizures at higher doses or in susceptible individuals. Do not stop abruptly. Avoid alcohol.

name: Tapentadol 50mg
description: A centrally-acting analgesic with dual mechanism: mu-opioid receptor agonist and norepinephrine reuptake inhibitor.
typicalUse: 1 tablet every 4-6 hours as directed. Extended release available for chronic use.
storage: Store securely at room temperature. Schedule II controlled substance.
warning: High abuse potential. Respiratory depression risk. Use only under strict medical supervision.

name: Buprenorphine 2mg
description: A partial mu-opioid receptor agonist with high potency and long duration. Used for severe chronic pain and opioid dependence.
typicalUse: Sublingual tablets or transdermal patches as per physician guidance.
storage: Store in secure location. Keep out of reach of children.
warning: Ceiling effect at high doses reduces overdose risk. Sublingual tablets must be dissolved - not swallowed.

name: Morphine Sulfate 10mg
description: The prototypical opioid analgesic. Gold standard for severe acute and chronic pain, especially palliative care.
typicalUse: Dose individualized by physician. Immediate release every 4 hours or sustained release every 12 hours.
storage: Schedule II opioid. Store under lock and key. Strict inventory maintained.
warning: STRICTLY controlled substance. Respiratory depression is primary risk. Naloxone reversal required nearby.

name: Codeine Phosphate 30mg
description: A mild to moderate opioid analgesic, often combined with paracetamol. Also a potent cough suppressant.
usedFor: Mild to Moderate Pain (often in combination products)
typicalUse: 1-2 tablets every 4-6 hours as directed. Commonly in combination with paracetamol.
storage: Controlled substance. Store securely below 30°C.
warning: CYP2D6 ultra-metabolizers risk overdose. Combination products limit paracetamol to 4g/day total.

name: Fentanyl Citrate 100mcg
description: An extremely potent synthetic opioid (100x morphine). Used in anesthesia and for breakthrough cancer pain.
typicalUse: ADMINISTERED BY HEALTH PROFESSIONAL ONLY. Various routes: IV, epidural, transdermal patch, lozenge.
storage: Schedule II. HIGHLY restricted. Hospital pharmacy control only.
warning: EXTREMELY POTENT. Life-threatening respiratory depression. STRICT medical supervision only. Overdose is fatal.

name: Aspirin 75mg (EC)
description: Antiplatelet medicine (low-dose) that prevents blood clots. Used ONLY for heart patients to reduce risk of heart attack and stroke. NOT for fever or general pain.
typicalUse: 1 tablet (75-150mg) once daily after food, as advised by cardiologist ONLY. Do NOT use for fever, headache or body pain.
storage: Store in cool, dry place. Protect from moisture (tablets hydrolyze).
warning: SIRF HEART PATIENTS KE LIYE HAI. Bukar, sir dard ya body pain ke liye mat use karein. Use Paracetamol 500mg instead. Stop 7 days before surgery only after consulting cardiologist.

name: Combiflam Tablet
description: Fixed dose combination of Ibuprofen 400mg + Paracetamol 325mg for synergistic relief from severe pain. NOT for simple fever - use Paracetamol 500mg.
typicalUse: 1 tablet every 6-8 hours after food. Maximum 3 tablets per day.
storage: Store at room temperature. Protect from light and moisture.
warning: Do not take with other paracetamol or NSAID products. Follow dose limits strictly.

name: Dolo 650 Paracetamol
description: Higher strength paracetamol (650mg) for extended relief from moderate to severe pain. For fever use Paracetamol 500mg.
typicalUse: 1 tablet every 8 hours as required. Maximum 4 tablets (2600mg) per day.
storage: Store at room temperature. Keep in original blister pack.
warning: Do not crush or split extended release tablets. Maintain minimum 8 hours between doses.

name: Crocin Advance
description: Fast-acting paracetamol 500mg formulation for pain. For fever, use standard Paracetamol 500mg tablet.
typicalUse: 1-2 tablets every 4-6 hours. Maximum 8 tablets per day.
storage: Store below 30°C. Protect from direct light.
warning: Do not take with any other paracetamol-containing product. Check for paracetamol in cough/cold combinations.

name: Sumo Pain Killer
description: Combination of Nimesulide 100mg + Paracetamol 325mg for rapid anti-inflammatory pain relief.
typicalUse: 1 tablet 2-3 times daily after meals. Short-term use only.
storage: Store in cool dry place. Protect from moisture.
warning: Avoid prolonged use. Monitor liver function with use >5 days. Not for children.

name: Nimesulide 100mg
description: A preferential COX-2 inhibitor NSAID with rapid onset. Used short-term for acute pain.
typicalUse: 1 tablet twice daily after food. Use for shortest period needed (max 15 days).
storage: Store below 25°C in original pack.
warning: BOXED WARNING: Hepatotoxicity risk. Shortest duration use only. Stop if any signs of liver dysfunction.

name: Ranitidine 150mg
description: A histamine H2-receptor antagonist that reduces stomach acid secretion. Used for acidity and ulcers.
typicalUse: 1 tablet twice daily (morning and bedtime) or 2 tablets at bedtime.
storage: Store at room temperature. Protect from light and moisture.
warning: Long-term use (>1 year) may have risks. Reassess periodically. Many formulations recalled due to NDMA impurity.

name: Omeprazole 20mg
description: A proton pump inhibitor (PPI) that provides powerful and prolonged suppression of gastric acid production.
typicalUse: 1 capsule once daily 30 minutes before breakfast. Severe cases: twice daily.
sideEffects: Long-term: B12 deficiency, bone density loss
storage: Store in cool place below 25°C. Protect from moisture.
warning: Take before eating. Long-term use requires monitoring of magnesium, B12, and bone health.

name: Pantoprazole 40mg
description: A proton pump inhibitor with high stability and efficacy in suppressing gastric acid secretion.
typicalUse: 1 tablet once daily 30 minutes before breakfast.
avoidIf: Severe liver impairment requires dose adjustment
storage: Store in original pack. Protect from light and moisture.
warning: Tablets must be swallowed whole, not crushed. PPI therapy increases fracture risk in elderly with long-term use.

name: Rabeprazole 20mg
description: A PPI with quick onset of action. Preferred for rapid symptom relief in acid-related disorders.
typicalUse: 1 tablet once daily, preferably in the morning, 15-30 minutes before food.
storage: Store below 30°C. Protect from moisture.
warning: Faster onset than other PPIs. May interfere with clopidogrel activation and vitamin B12 absorption.

name: Esomeprazole 40mg
description: The S-isomer of omeprazole. More potent and predictable acid suppression than racemic omeprazole.
typicalUse: 1 capsule once daily 30-60 minutes before the largest meal.
storage: Store below 25°C in original package.
warning: Use lowest effective dose. Monitor magnesium levels in patients on long-term therapy (>3 months).

name: Gelusil MPS
description: A combination antacid (aluminum hydroxide + magnesium hydroxide + simethicone) for rapid relief of acidity and gas.
typicalUse: 2 teaspoons (suspension) or 1-2 tablets chewed after meals and at bedtime.
storage: Store at room temperature. Shake suspension well before use.
warning: Rapid but short-acting. Do not take within 2 hours of other medications (reduces absorption).

name: Digene Gel (Mint)
description: A popular flavored oral antacid gel containing magnesium hydroxide, aluminum hydroxide, simethicone, and sodium carboxymethylcellulose.
typicalUse: 2 teaspoonfuls (10ml) 4 times a day after meals and at night. Chew tablets well.
storage: Store below 30°C. Do not freeze.
warning: Quick relief for occasional acidity. Chronic symptoms need medical evaluation, not just antacids.

name: Pan-D (Pantoprazole + Domperidone)
description: Combination of Pantoprazole 40mg (enteric coated) + Domperidone 30mg (SR). Relieves acidity AND nausea/bloating.
typicalUse: 1 capsule once daily on empty stomach, 15-30 minutes before breakfast.
storage: Store in cool, dry place. Blister integrity important.
warning: Capsule must be swallowed whole (contains SR beads). Long-term domperidone use has cardiac risks.

name: Domperidone 10mg
description: A dopamine antagonist that works as an anti-emetic and promotes gastric emptying. Does not cross blood-brain barrier easily.
typicalUse: 1 tablet 3-4 times daily 15-30 minutes before meals.
storage: Store below 25°C. Protect from light.
warning: Use at lowest effective dose. Avoid co-administration with QT-prolonging drugs like erythromycin.

name: Ondansetron 4mg MD
description: A selective 5-HT3 receptor antagonist. Very effective for controlling nausea and vomiting from various causes.
typicalUse: 1 tablet (MD dissolves on tongue) 30 minutes before triggering event. Repeat every 4-8 hours as needed.
storage: Store in original pack. Protect from moisture.
warning: MD tablet: do not swallow whole - let dissolve on tongue. Monitor for serotonin syndrome with SSRIs.

name: ORS (Oral Rehydration Salts)
description: WHO-ORS formula (low osmolarity) with balanced glucose-sodium to maximize intestinal water absorption.
typicalUse: Dissolve 1 sachet in 1 liter of clean drinking water. Drink small amounts frequently. 50-100ml/kg for dehydration.
storage: Store sachets in cool dry place. Prepared solution: discard after 24 hours.
warning: Dissolve ONLY in 1 liter water. Do not add sugar/salt. Give sip-by-sip for vomiting patients.

name: Loperamide 2mg
description: An opioid receptor agonist that slows intestinal motility and reduces fluid secretion into the bowel.
typicalUse: 2 capsules initially, then 1 capsule after each loose stool. Maximum 8 capsules/day (16mg).
storage: Store at room temperature. Protect from moisture.
warning: DO NOT use in bloody diarrhea or high fever (infection needs to be treated). Use for short duration only.

name: Racecadotril 100mg
description: An enkephalinase inhibitor that reduces intestinal hypersecretion without slowing motility. Better tolerated than loperamide.
typicalUse: 1 capsule 3 times daily before meals until diarrhea stops. Max 7 days.
storage: Store below 30°C in original blister.
warning: Does not paralyze gut like loperamide. Better for secretory diarrhea. Always combine with ORS.

name: Ofloxacin + Ornidazole
description: Combination fluoroquinolone + nitroimidazole antibiotic for treating mixed bacterial and protozoal GI infections.
typicalUse: 1 tablet twice daily for 3-5 days as prescribed. Take with food.
storage: Store at room temperature protected from light.
warning: ANTIBIOTIC: Complete full course. Avoid sunlight. STRICTLY NO ALCOHOL during and 3 days after.

name: Metronidazole 400mg
description: A nitroimidazole antibacterial and antiprotozoal. Highly active against anaerobic bacteria and parasites.
typicalUse: 1 tablet 3 times daily after food for 5-10 days as prescribed.
storage: Store in light-resistant container below 30°C.
warning: STRICTLY AVOID ALL ALCOHOL during treatment and 3 DAYS AFTER. Causes vomiting, flushing, palpitations.

name: Cetirizine 10mg
description: A second-generation non-sedating (slightly sedating) antihistamine H1-receptor blocker for allergies.
typicalUse: 1 tablet once daily. Can take at bedtime if mild drowsiness occurs.
storage: Store at room temperature. Protect from light and moisture.
warning: May cause drowsiness. Caution when driving or operating machinery. Avoid alcohol.

name: Levocetirizine 5mg
description: The active levo-isomer of cetirizine. Effective at half the dose with slightly less sedation.
typicalUse: 1 tablet once daily, preferably in the evening.
storage: Store below 25°C in original blister pack.
warning: Avoid concurrent use of CNS depressants and alcohol. Take in evening if daytime drowsiness occurs.

name: Fexofenadine 120mg
description: A truly non-sedating second-generation antihistamine. Preferred for daytime use when alertness is required.
typicalUse: 1 tablet once daily on an empty stomach. Do not take with fruit juice.
storage: Store in original package below 25°C.
warning: Do NOT take with grapefruit, orange, or apple juice - reduces absorption by 30-60%. Non-sedating option.

name: Chlorpheniramine Maleate 4mg (CPM)
description: Classic first-generation sedating antihistamine. Common in combination cold products. Very effective for urticaria.
typicalUse: 1 tablet 3-4 times daily or at bedtime for night-time relief.
storage: Store below 30°C protected from light.
warning: Strong sedation. Do NOT drive or operate machinery. Avoid alcohol. Not preferred for daily use.

name: Montelukast 10mg
description: A leukotriene receptor antagonist. Prevents allergic airway inflammation and reduces asthma/allergy symptoms.
typicalUse: 1 tablet once daily in the evening (asthma) or any time for allergic rhinitis.
storage: Store at room temperature in original pack.
warning: Not for acute asthma attacks. Monitor for mood/behavior changes, especially in pediatric patients.

name: Hydroxyzine 10mg
description: A first-generation antihistamine with additional anxiolytic (anti-anxiety) and sedative properties.
typicalUse: 1 tablet 2-4 times daily as prescribed. Sedation is common - typically taken at night.
storage: Store below 30°C. Protect from light.
warning: Strong sedation. Avoid activities requiring mental alertness. Do not combine with alcohol or benzodiazepines.

name: Vicks VapoRub
description: Topical ointment containing camphor, menthol, and eucalyptus oil. Provides symptomatic relief of cold symptoms through inhalation.
typicalUse: Rub thick layer on chest, throat, and back. Cover with warm cloth if desired. For steam inhalation: add 1 tsp to hot water.
storage: Store below 30°C with lid tightly closed. Melted ointment solidifies again on cooling.
warning: FOR EXTERNAL USE ONLY. Never ingest or apply inside nostrils. Camphor is toxic if swallowed.

name: Ambroxol 30mg
description: A mucolytic agent that thins and loosens mucus (phlegm) in the airways, making it easier to cough out.
typicalUse: 1 tablet or 1 teaspoon syrup 3 times daily with plenty of fluids.
storage: Store in cool dry place. Syrup may need refrigeration after opening (check label).
warning: Drink PLENTY OF WATER - it helps the mucolytic work. NOT for dry cough (do not suppress productive cough).

name: Dextromethorphan 10mg (DXM)
description: A centrally-acting cough suppressant (antitussive) that reduces the urge to cough without being a narcotic.
typicalUse: As per syrup/tablet directions. Typically every 6-8 hours as needed.
storage: Store below 30°C. Keep syrup tightly capped.
warning: ABUSE POTENTIAL. Keep out of reach of teens. Do not use for productive cough with mucus - that should be cleared.

name: Guaifenesin + Phenylephrine (Combination)
description: Combination cold remedy: expectorant (guaifenesin) + decongestant (phenylephrine) often with paracetamol.
typicalUse: 5-10ml syrup 3 times daily as directed. Shake bottle well.
storage: Store below 30°C. Protect from light.
warning: Read ingredients to avoid doubling up on paracetamol from other medicines. Can raise blood pressure.

name: Azithromycin 500mg
description: A broad-spectrum macrolide antibiotic with once-daily dosing and excellent tissue penetration.
typicalUse: 1 tablet once daily. Common course: 3-5 days (varies by condition). Z-pack = 500mg day 1, then 250mg x 4 days.
avoidIf: History of cholestatic jaundice with azithromycin
storage: Store below 30°C. Keep in original blister.
warning: ANTIBIOTIC. COMPLETE FULL COURSE. Even once-daily - don't miss doses. Can react with warfarin. May cause heart rhythm changes.

name: Amoxicillin 500mg
description: A widely-used penicillin-class beta-lactam antibiotic. Effective against many common bacterial infections.
typicalUse: 1 capsule 3 times daily (every 8 hours) for 5-7 days as prescribed.
storage: Refrigerate suspension. Capsules at room temperature protected from moisture.
warning: Seek emergency help for rash, swelling, or breathing difficulty (anaphylaxis). Antibiotic - complete full course.

name: Ciprofloxacin 500mg
description: A broad-spectrum fluoroquinolone antibiotic with good activity against Gram-negative organisms.
typicalUse: 1 tablet twice daily for 3-14 days depending on infection type.
storage: Store below 30°C protected from light.
warning: BOXED WARNING: Tendinitis/tendon rupture risk (especially Achilles, >60yrs, with steroids). Avoid direct sunlight. Hydrate well.

name: Cefixime 200mg
description: An oral third-generation cephalosporin antibiotic with excellent Gram-negative coverage including typhoid.
typicalUse: 1 tablet twice daily (or 2 tablets once daily) for 3-14 days depending on infection.
avoidIf: Severe renal failure without dose adjustment
storage: Store at room temperature. Keep in original container.
warning: Cross-allergy with penicillins in ~10% of patients. Complete antibiotic course as prescribed.

name: Doxycycline 100mg
description: A lipophilic tetracycline with broad-spectrum activity, also used as anti-inflammatory and for malaria prophylaxis.
typicalUse: 100mg twice daily on day 1, then 100mg once daily. Always with a full glass of water.
storage: Store below 30°C protected from light and moisture.
warning: ESOPHAGEAL DAMAGE RISK: sit upright for 30 min after taking, do NOT take before bed. SEVERE SUNBURN RISK - use SPF 50+.

name: Nitrofurantoin 100mg
description: A urinary tract-specific antibiotic. Concentrates in urine and is first-line for uncomplicated cystitis.
typicalUse: 1 tablet 4 times daily or 100mg MR twice daily for 5-7 days. With food.
storage: Store in cool dry place below 25°C.
warning: URINE TURNS BROWN - do not be alarmed. Take with food. Long-term use requires periodic pulmonary follow-up.

name: Clotrimazole Cream 1%
description: Broad-spectrum imidazole antifungal for topical use against candidiasis and dermatophytes.
typicalUse: Apply thin layer 2-3 times daily to affected area. Continue 1-2 weeks after symptoms resolve to prevent relapse.
storage: Store below 30°C. Do not freeze.
warning: Keep using FULL COURSE even after symptoms clear. Ringworm needs 2-4 weeks. Do not bandage too tightly.

name: Fluconazole 150mg
description: A triazole-class oral antifungal with excellent bioavailability and safety. First-line for vaginal candidiasis.
typicalUse: Vaginal candidiasis: single 150mg dose. Other conditions: duration varies by site (1-4 weeks).
storage: Store below 30°C. Protect from light and moisture.
warning: Single-dose therapy for yeast infection - if symptoms persist >3 days see a doctor. Multiple drug interactions.

name: Itraconazole 100mg
description: A lipophilic triazole antifungal with excellent activity against dermatophytes, yeast, and some molds.
food: After food (full meal critical for absorption)
typicalUse: Nail fungus: pulse therapy or daily dosing over months. Requires LFT monitoring.
storage: Store in original pack below 25°C.
warning: TAKE WITH FULL MEAL or absorption drops dramatically. Hepatotoxicity risk: LFTs at baseline and monthly for long courses.

name: Terbinafine 250mg
description: An allylamine antifungal drug. Drug of choice for dermatophyte onychomycosis (nail fungus) in many guidelines.
typicalUse: Fingernails: 250mg daily x 6 weeks. Toenails: 250mg daily x 12 weeks. Topical for minor skin fungal.
storage: Store below 30°C in original packaging.
warning: Long therapy (3+ months). LFTs at baseline and 4 weeks in. Taste disturbance may persist weeks after stopping.

name: Permethrin Cream 5%
description: A synthetic pyrethroid pediculicide/scabicide. Gold-standard topical treatment for scabies and head lice.
typicalUse: Scabies: apply thin layer FULL BODY (neck to toes including nails/skin folds), leave 8-14hrs, then wash off. Repeat after 7 days.
storage: Store below 30°C. Keep out of eyes, nose, mouth.
warning: ENTIRE HOUSEHOLD must treat simultaneously. Bedding/clothes laundered in hot water. Itching may persist 2 weeks (dead mites/allergic).

name: Benzoyl Peroxide 2.5% Gel
description: A non-antibiotic acne treatment with bactericidal (Cutibacterium acnes), comedolytic, and mild anti-inflammatory effects.
typicalUse: Apply thin layer to affected area(s) once daily initially, then increase to twice daily if tolerated.
storage: Store below 30°C. FLAMMABLE: keep away from fire.
warning: Start slowly (once daily). SUN SENSITIVITY. BLEACHES CLOTHING/BED SHEETS - allow to fully dry before contact. Wash hands after.

name: Clindamycin Phosphate 1% Gel
description: Topical lincosamide antibiotic. Reduces C. acnes and inflammatory papules/pustules. Typically combined with benzoyl peroxide.
typicalUse: Thin layer to affected areas twice daily. Always use in combination with benzoyl peroxide (reduces resistance).
sideEffects: Rare: C. diff diarrhea (systemic absorption rare)
storage: Store below 30°C. Avoid freezing.
warning: RESISTANCE RISK if used without benzoyl peroxide. Do not use long-term as monotherapy. Avoid eyes/mouth.

name: Adapalene 0.1% Gel
description: A third-generation topical retinoid. Normalizes keratinization to prevent comedones (whiteheads/blackheads).
typicalUse: Apply pea-sized amount to entire face at night, after cleansing. Sun protection mandatory in daytime.
avoidIf: Concurrent use with other harsh exfoliants
storage: Store below 25°C. Avoid light exposure.
warning: SUN PROTECTION EVERY MORNING IS NON-NEGOTIABLE. Start 2-3 nights/week then increase. Purge is NORMAL for first 6 weeks.

name: Calamine Lotion
description: A soothing skin protectant and mild antipruritic. Zinc oxide + ferric oxide suspension. Often with calamine or aloe.
typicalUse: Shake well. Apply liberally to affected area 3-4 times daily as needed. Let dry (forms pink protective layer).
storage: Store below 30°C. Shake well before each use.
warning: For EXTERNAL USE ONLY. Pink stain will wash off skin but be careful with clothing/linen.

name: Hydrocortisone 1% Cream
description: Lowest potency topical corticosteroid. Safe OTC for short periods on eczema, insect bites, mild rashes.
typicalUse: Apply thin layer 2-3 times daily for maximum 7 days on face, 14 days on body. Rub in gently.
storage: Store below 30°C. Do not freeze.
warning: SHORT DURATION ONLY. Never use on undiagnosed rash that could be fungal (ringworm). Avoid broken skin absorption.

name: Beclomethasone Cream
description: Medium potency topical corticosteroid for more extensive or resistant inflammatory dermatoses.
typicalUse: Thin layer 1-2 times daily. Avoid face, groin, axillae unless specifically instructed. Maximum 2 weeks course.
storage: Store at room temperature below 30°C.
warning: USE ONLY AS DIRECTED. Do not occlude unless told. Use smallest amount needed. Never on the face without prescription.

name: Mometasone 0.1% Cream
description: High-potency once-daily topical corticosteroid with strong anti-inflammatory and antipruritic effects.
typicalUse: Once-daily application. Thin film. Shortest duration possible. Never face/groin/axillae.
storage: Store below 25°C. Protect from light.
warning: HIGH POTENCY. Once daily only. Never on face or flexures. Do NOT use >2 consecutive weeks on any site.

name: Clobetasol Propionate 0.05%
description: Super-potent topical corticosteroid (Class I). Use only for short courses and very limited areas of severe dermatoses.
typicalUse: Apply sparingly 1-2 times daily for MAXIMUM 2 weeks, then step down. Never on face/axillae/groin.
avoidIf: Any area other than thick palms/soles/scalp
storage: Store below 30°C. Light-resistant.
warning: SUPER-POTENT. RISK OF PERMANENT SKIN DAMAGE. NEVER USE BEYOND 2 WEEKS. USE ONLY WHERE PRESCRIBED.

name: Salicylic Acid 6% Ointment
description: A keratolytic agent that softens and removes excess keratin. Used for warts, corns, and thick scaly conditions.
typicalUse: Apply carefully ONLY to lesion (protect surrounding skin with petroleum jelly). 1-2 times daily until resolution (weeks).
storage: Store at room temperature. Keep away from eyes.
warning: PROTECT SURROUNDING HEALTHY SKIN. Stop if severe pain occurs. Persistent warts after 3 months need cryotherapy.

name: Acyclovir Eye Ointment 3%
description: Nucleoside analogue antiviral. Ophthalmic preparation specifically for herpes simplex keratitis of the eye.
typicalUse: 1 cm ribbon into lower conjunctival sac, 5 times daily (every 4 hours while awake). Continue 3 days after healing.
storage: Store below 25°C. Do not freeze. Tip should not touch eye.
warning: If symptoms do not improve in 24-48 hours SEE OPHTHALMOLOGIST IMMEDIATELY. Vision-threatening infection.

name: Chloramphenicol Eye Drops 0.5%
description: Broad-spectrum bacteriostatic antibiotic eye preparation for superficial bacterial eye infections.
typicalUse: 1-2 drops into affected eye(s) every 2-4 hours for first 2 days, then 4 times daily. 5-7 day course.
sideEffects: Bone marrow suppression (EXTREMELY RARE with topical use)
storage: Store in refrigerator. Discard 4 weeks after opening.
warning: SEE EYE DOCTOR if vision affected, severe pain, photophobia, or no improvement after 2 days. Not for contact lens wearers during treatment.

name: Carboxymethylcellulose Eye Drops 0.5%
description: Lubricating artificial tear substitute with carboxymethylcellulose. Relieves dry eyes and eye strain.
typicalUse: 1-2 drops in each eye as often as needed. Preservative-free unit doses for frequent use (>4 times/day).
storage: Store below 30°C. Single-use vials discard after each use.
warning: Multidose bottles: discard 4 weeks after opening. If dryness persists >1 week with drops, get eye exam for underlying cause.

name: Sodium Chloride Nasal Spray 0.9%
description: Isotonic saline solution for nasal hygiene. Moistens nasal passages and flushes out mucus, dust, and allergens.
typicalUse: 2-3 sprays per nostril 3-4 times daily. Blow nose gently afterwards.
storage: Store below 30°C. Discard 4 weeks after opening.
warning: SAFE for ALL ages. Can be used alongside medication. Most effective first step for blocked nose before decongestants.

name: Xylometazoline Nasal Drops 0.1%
description: Imidazoline alpha-adrenergic agonist. Potent vasoconstrictor. Reduces nasal swelling rapidly.
typicalUse: 2-3 drops per nostril, every 8-12 hours. MAXIMUM DURATION OF USE: 5-7 DAYS ONLY.
sideEffects: RHINITIS MEDICAMENTOSA (Rebound Congestion if used >7 days)
storage: Store below 30°C. Protect from light.
warning: MAX 5-7 DAYS USE ONLY. LONGER USE CAUSES PERMANENT REBOUND STUFFY NOSE. Extremely common misuse complication.

name: Oxymetazoline Nasal Spray 0.05%
description: Long-acting imidazoline decongestant. Up to 12 hours of relief per dose. Same rebound risk.
typicalUse: 2-3 sprays per nostril twice daily (morning & bedtime). STRICTLY 3-5 DAY LIMIT.
storage: Store below 25°C.
warning: REBOUND CONGESTION after 3-5 days use is the main risk. Stop after 3 days maximum. Use saline instead for longer courses.

name: Waxolve Ear Drops
description: Carbamide peroxide (urea hydrogen peroxide) ear drops. Effervesces and softens impacted cerumen (ear wax).
typicalUse: 5-10 drops in affected ear, lie on side 5-10 minutes. Twice daily for 3-7 days. Then irrigation at clinic.
sideEffects: Temporary hearing loss if foam blocks canal
storage: Store below 30°C. Avoid heating.
warning: IF EAR DRUM IS PERFORATED, DROPS ARE DANGEROUS. Do not use if ear is discharging pus or blood - see ENT first.

name: Lidocaine 2% Jelly
description: Topical local anesthetic jelly. Numbs surface on contact. Used for urethral anesthesia, minor procedures, and surface pain.
typicalUse: Apply thin layer to affected area 15-30 minutes before procedure or as directed for symptomatic relief.
sideEffects: Toxicity (large doses on mucous membranes: seizures, arrhythmia)
storage: Store below 30°C. Protect from light.
warning: Do not use on large areas or deep wounds (systemic absorption). Not on eyes. Keep away from children.

name: Nifedipine 20mg (SR)
description: Dihydropyridine calcium channel blocker. Peripheral vasodilator used for hypertension and angina.
typicalUse: As prescribed. SR formulations usually twice daily. Do NOT break or crush sustained release tablets.
storage: Store below 30°C. Protect from light. SR tablets: do not split.
warning: AVOID GRAPEFRUIT JUICE (3x bioavailability increase). Do not discontinue abruptly - rebound hypertension possible.

name: Amlodipine 5mg
description: Long-acting dihydropyridine calcium channel blocker. Once-daily oral antihypertensive/antianginal.
typicalUse: 1 tablet once daily. Titrate up to 10mg if needed. Very long half-life - consistent once daily dosing.
storage: Store at room temperature below 30°C.
warning: Ankle swelling is dose-related - elevate feet or consult if persistent. Most commonly prescribed BP medication in India.

name: Atenolol 50mg
description: A cardio-selective beta-1 adrenergic receptor blocker. Reduces heart rate, BP, and cardiac workload.
typicalUse: 1 tablet once daily (or twice if higher doses). Do NOT stop abruptly.
storage: Store in cool dry place. Protect from light.
warning: DO NOT STOP ABRUPTLY - severe rebound hypertension/angina. Must taper over 1-2 weeks. Check heart rate before dosing.

name: Metoprolol Succinate 50mg (XL)
description: Selective beta-1 blocker extended release formulation. Preferred in stable chronic heart failure guidelines.
typicalUse: 1 tablet once daily in the morning. Dose individualized carefully in heart failure (start low, go slow).
storage: Store below 25°C. Do not crush XL beads.
warning: XL tablet may be split along score line but NOT chewed/crushed. Heart failure patients: start very low dose.

name: Lisinopril 10mg
description: A long-acting ACE inhibitor antihypertensive. Also cardioprotective in heart failure and post-MI.
typicalUse: 1 tablet once daily. Titrate slowly. Monitor renal function and potassium periodically.
storage: Store in cool dry place below 25°C.
warning: IF YOU BECOME PREGNANT STOP IMMEDIATELY. Dry cough is not allergic - report to doctor for alternative (ARB). Angioedema = ER visit.

name: Losartan 50mg
description: Angiotensin II receptor blocker (ARB). Similar benefits to ACE inhibitors but WITHOUT the dry cough.
typicalUse: 1 tablet once daily. Some patients need twice daily dosing.
storage: Store below 30°C in original pack.
warning: TERATOGENIC in 2nd/3rd trimester - pregnancy test before start. No cough (unlike ACEi). Uric acid lowering side benefit.

name: Telmisartan 40mg
description: Longest half-life ARB. PPAR-gamma agonist activity gives mild metabolic benefits. Excellent cardioprotective profile.
typicalUse: 1 tablet once daily. Very long half-life (24h+) so once daily is effective for 24-hour BP control.
storage: Store in original pack below 30°C.
warning: Dosing time not as critical - very long half-life. Preferred ARB in patients with metabolic syndrome.

name: Hydrochlorothiazide 12.5mg
description: A thiazide diuretic antihypertensive. Increases sodium and water excretion. Often combined with ACEi/ARB.
typicalUse: 1 tablet once daily in the MORNING (so it doesn't disrupt sleep with nighttime urination).
storage: Store below 30°C. Protect from light and moisture.
warning: Take in the MORNING. Eat potassium-rich foods (banana, coconut water). Monitor serum electrolytes periodically.

name: Atorvastatin 20mg
description: Most commonly prescribed statin. Potent HMG-CoA reductase inhibitor lowering LDL cholesterol by ~38-50% at 20mg.
typicalUse: 1 tablet once daily in the EVENING (cholesterol synthesis peaks at night - though atorvastatin long half-life is flexible).
storage: Store below 30°C. Protect from light.
warning: Report UNEXPLAINED MUSCLE PAIN, WEAKNESS or BROWN URINE immediately (possible rhabdomyolysis). LFTs at baseline.

name: Rosuvastatin 10mg
description: The most potent statin (per mg). Highest LDL reduction (~50% at 10-20mg). Approved for high-intensity therapy.
typicalUse: 1 tablet once daily at any time. Dose titrated based on LDL response every 2-4 weeks.
storage: Store below 25°C in original container.
warning: Highest potency statin. Monitor CK if muscle symptoms. More drug interactions with protease inhibitors.

name: Aspirin 75mg + Clopidogrel 75mg
description: Dual antiplatelet therapy (DAPT). Aspirin + thienopyridine P2Y12 inhibitor. Standard after coronary stent/MI.
typicalUse: 1 tablet once daily. Duration of DAPT variable: 1-12 months or longer depending on stent and procedure.
avoidIf: Surgery (must inform surgeon - stop 5-7 days pre-op)
storage: Store below 30°C. Keep in original blister.
warning: BLEEDING RISK: Blood in stool (black, tarry), blood in urine, excessive bruising - report immediately. DO NOT STOP WITHOUT CARDIOLOGIST ADVICE.

name: Metformin 500mg (SR)
description: First-line oral anti-diabetic drug. Improves insulin sensitivity and reduces hepatic glucose production.
typicalUse: Start low: 500mg SR once daily with dinner, then titrate up. Target dose typically 1500-2000mg/day in divided doses.
sideEffects: DIARRHEA / GI UPSET (common initially, transient - SR + after meals helps)
storage: Store below 25°C. Protect from moisture.
warning: GI side effects fade in 2-4 weeks - persistence not normal. LACTIC ACIDOSIS rare but serious (weakness, muscle pain, dyspnea).

name: Glimepiride 2mg
description: A third-generation sulfonylurea. Stimulates pancreatic beta-cell insulin secretion. Hypoglycemia risk.
typicalUse: 1 tablet once daily with the FIRST main meal of the day. Monitor blood glucose. Hypoglycemia possible.
sideEffects: HYPOGLYCEMIA (serious risk - symptoms: sweating, trembling, hunger, confusion)
storage: Store below 30°C in original pack.
warning: HYPOGLYCEMIA RISK: Always carry sugar/glucose tablets with you. Do not skip meals. Take with largest meal.

name: Vildagliptin 50mg + Metformin 1000mg
description: Fixed-dose combination of DPP-4 inhibitor (gliptin) + metformin. Low hypoglycemia risk. Good tolerability.
typicalUse: 1 tablet twice daily after meals. Single-pill combination for convenience.
storage: Store below 30°C. Protect from moisture.
warning: Pancreatitis risk (rare - severe abdominal pain). Low hypoglycemia risk compared to sulfonylureas.

name: Levothyroxine 100mcg
description: Synthetic levo-isomer of thyroxine (T4). Replaces or supplements natural thyroid hormone in hypothyroidism.
typicalUse: 1 tablet once daily FIRST THING IN THE MORNING, ON EMPTY STOMACH, 30-60 MINUTES BEFORE FOOD/BEVERAGES/OTHER MEDS.
sideEffects: Overdose = HYPERTHYROID (palpitations, anxiety, weight loss, tremor)
storage: Store below 25°C. Protect from LIGHT and MOISTURE (degrades easily).
warning: EMPTY STOMACH 30-60 MINUTES BEFORE ANYTHING ELSE. No calcium/iron/antacids for 4 hours after. TSH checked after 6-8 weeks.

name: Multivitamin (B-Complex + Minerals)
description: Broad-spectrum B-complex vitamins with minerals. Supports energy metabolism, immunity, and general health.
typicalUse: 1 tablet/capsule once daily after the largest meal of the day for best absorption.
storage: Store in cool, dry place below 25°C. Protect from light.
warning: Does NOT replace balanced diet. B2 makes urine bright YELLOW - not alarming. Consult if on other specific supplements.

name: Vitamin D3 60,000 IU (Cholecalciferol)
description: Weekly mega-dose of vitamin D3. Corrects vitamin D deficiency which is highly prevalent in Indian subcontinent.
food: With fat containing meal (vitamin D fat-soluble)
typicalUse: 1 sachet/capsule once WEEKLY (every 7 days) for 8 weeks (loading), then once monthly for maintenance.
sideEffects: Hypercalcemia symptoms (excess: nausea, confusion, thirst, kidney stones)
storage: Store below 25°C. Protect from light.
warning: WEEKLY DOSE, not daily. Take with fat-containing food for absorption. Check serum 25(OH)D levels after 3 months.

name: Vitamin B12 (Methylcobalamin 1500mcg)
description: Active form of vitamin B12. Critical for nerve function, red cell formation, and DNA synthesis. Vegans/vegetarians often deficient.
typicalUse: 1 tablet/capsule once daily sublingually (under tongue) for best absorption. For severe deficiency: parenteral loading first.
storage: Store below 25°C. Protect from light and moisture.
warning: Deficiency common in VEGANS/VEGETARIANS (B12 only from animal foods). Absorption decreases with age. Check levels + folate.

name: Calcium Citrate 1000mg + Vitamin D3
description: Well-absorbed calcium citrate formulation combined with vitamin D3 for bone health. Better tolerated than carbonate.
food: Either (citrate better absorbed on empty stomach than carbonate)
typicalUse: 1-2 tablets daily after meals divided into doses (max 500-600mg elemental calcium absorbed at once).
sideEffects: Hypercalcemia (excess) with risk of kidney stones
storage: Store below 30°C. Protect from moisture.
warning: Divide doses (500-600mg max absorbed at one time). Drink adequate water (reduces stone risk). Vitamin D needed for absorption.

name: Alprazolam 0.5mg
description: Short-acting benzodiazepine anxiolytic. Rapidly relieves acute anxiety, panic attacks, and situational anxiety.
typicalUse: As prescribed for SHORT COURSE only. 0.25-0.5mg 3 times daily for anxiety; typically maximum 4mg/day divided.
storage: Schedule IV drug. Store securely below 30°C.
warning: HIGH DEPENDENCE & ADDICTION POTENTIAL. SHORT-TERM USE ONLY (2-4 weeks). DO NOT STOP ABRUPTLY. NO ALCOHOL. AVOID DRIVING.

name: Zolpidem 10mg
description: Non-benzodiazepine hypnotic ('Z-drug'). Rapid onset short-duration sleep aid with minimal next-day drowsiness.
typicalUse: 1 tablet IMMEDIATELY BEFORE BEDTIME on empty stomach. SHORT-TERM USE ONLY (2-4 weeks max). Immediately get into bed.
sideEffects: Complex sleep behaviors (sleep walking/eating - rare but serious)
storage: Controlled substance. Store securely below 30°C.
warning: TAKE ONLY WHEN YOU CAN GET 7-8 HOURS UNINTERRUPTED SLEEP. Do not take with food/dairy (slows onset). Risk of sleepwalking/complex behaviors.

name: Escitalopram 10mg
description: Selective serotonin reuptake inhibitor (SSRI). First-line antidepressant and anxiolytic with good tolerability profile.
typicalUse: 1 tablet once daily (morning preferred if insomnia, evening if sedation). Start 5mg, then 10mg. 2-4 weeks onset.
storage: Store below 30°C. Protect from light.
warning: DO NOT STOP ABRUPTLY (discontinuation syndrome: brain zaps, dizziness, nausea). SUICIDAL THINKING MONITOR in <25yo. Works after 2-4 WEEKS.

name: Sertraline 50mg
description: Highly selective SSRI with multiple indications. Good first-line choice for depression with comorbid anxiety or OCD.
typicalUse: 1 tablet once daily with food (improves tolerability). Morning dose preferred. Titrate as needed over weeks.
storage: Store at room temperature protected from light.
warning: 2-4 WEEK ONSET. Do not miss doses. Serotonin syndrome risk with triptans, tramadol. Monitor worsening depression/suicidality early treatment.

name: Paracetamol + Phenylephrine + CPM (Cold Total)
description: Complete cold/flu relief combination: Paracetamol 500mg (pain/fever) + Phenylephrine (decongestant) + Chlorpheniramine (antihistamine).
typicalUse: 1 tablet 3-4 times daily after meals. Maximum 4 tablets in 24 hours. 3-5 day course typically.
storage: Store below 30°C. Protect from moisture.
warning: SEDATION from CPM component. Do not double up with separate paracetamol. Do not take if already taking other cold combinations.

name: Pudin Hara (Active)
description: Popular Ayurvedic preparation containing menthol, mint oil, and caraway oil. Fast-acting digestive aid for gas and spasms.
typicalUse: 1-2 capsules with water or 10-15 drops mixed in half cup water. Can repeat every 4 hours if needed.
storage: Store below 25°C. Volatile oils - keep tightly closed.
warning: Avoid in GERD as mint relaxes the esophageal sphincter and can worsen reflux.

name: Hajmola (Regular)
description: Traditional Ayurvedic digestive chewable tablets. Blend of herbs like ginger, long pepper, black pepper, and rock salt.
typicalUse: Chew 1-2 tablets after meals. Salted/sour taste stimulates digestive enzymes.
storage: Store in cool dry place. Keep lid tightly closed.
warning: HIGH SODIUM - avoid if on salt restricted diet. Appetite stimulant effect - caution in obesity/diabetes.

name: ORS-L (Orange Flavor)
description: WHO-formulated low osmolarity oral rehydration salts with improved orange flavor. Preferred for children and acute diarrhea.
typicalUse: Dissolve powder in 1 liter of clean drinking water. Give frequently in small sips. Continue breastfeeding infants.
sideEffects: None at correct dilution. Hypernatremia if made too concentrated.
storage: Store sachets in cool dry place. Prepared solution: discard unused portion after 24 hours.
warning: NEVER add extra sugar or salt. Dissolve fully in EXACTLY 1 liter water. If patient can't keep down due to vomiting, sip-by-sip 5-10 min intervals.

name: Telmisartan 40mg + Amlodipine 5mg
description: First-line recommended single-pill combination for hypertension. ARB + CCB. Powerful BP control with complementary mechanisms.
usedFor: Hypertension not controlled on single drug
typicalUse: 1 tablet once daily at any time of day (same time each day).
sideEffects: Peripheral edema (less than amlodipine alone - ARB counteracts)
avoidIf: Unilateral renal artery stenosis on solitary kidney
storage: Store below 25°C. Protect from light.
warning: ARB = STOP IF PREGNANT. Amlodipine ankle edema partially counteracted by telmisartan. Monitor BP regularly.

name: Sildenafil Citrate 50mg
description: Phosphodiesterase type 5 inhibitor. Used for erectile dysfunction and pulmonary arterial hypertension (different brand names).
typicalUse: 1 tablet 30-60 minutes before sexual activity. Maximum once daily. Sexual stimulation required.
avoidIf: ANY NITRATE USE (absolute contraindication - SEVERE HYPOTENSION, DEATH)
Non-arteritic anterior ischemic optic neuropathy history
storage: Store below 30°C. Protected from light and moisture.
warning: ABSOLUTELY NEVER USE WITH NITRATES (nitroglycerin, isosorbide) - FATAL HYPOTENSION. Do not combine with alpha blockers without dose adjustment.

name: Phenylephrine + CPM + Dextromethorphan Syrup
description: Cough-cold syrup: decongestant + antihistamine + cough suppressant combination. For severe dry/nocturnal cough due to cold.
typicalUse: 5-10ml syrup 3-4 times daily as directed. Not for children under 4 years without pediatrician advice.
storage: Store below 30°C. Protect from light. Shake well before use.
warning: DO NOT exceed 4 doses in 24 hours. Do not use for productive (wet) cough with mucus - use mucolytic instead.

name: Betadine 10% Solution
description: Broad-spectrum topical antiseptic with povidone-iodine. Kills bacteria, viruses, fungi, spores. Used for wound disinfection.
typicalUse: Apply full-strength to affected area 1-3 times daily. May be used wet or allowed to dry. Cover with dressing if needed.
sideEffects: Rare systemic absorption with large wounds
storage: Store below 30°C. Keep away from eyes and face. FLAMMABLE if mixed with alcohol solutions.
warning: FOR EXTERNAL USE ONLY. If applied to large open wounds for long periods, monitor thyroid function. Stains skin and fabrics.
